errorCodes.meaning: The caller administers no namespace — they hold neither the community-administrator capability nor a live, explicitly recorded `git.ns.admin` — or `namespace` names one they do not administer or one this VTC does not have. The three are answered alike, so the code cannot be used to learn which namespaces exist.

Bootstrap.description: Whether each step that turns commit trust on for a repository is in place, as last reported. A step that this forge's plan does not need reads `true`.

keyring.description: The exempt platform keyring for forge-signed merge commits is committed, or the forge's plan does not need one.

requiredCheck.description: The forge refuses to merge into the default branch unless the verify-trust check passes, with no bypass, and a pull request cannot change what that check runs: an organisation-required workflow, code-owner review of workflow files, or protected workflow paths, as the forge allows.

variables.description: The repository names the Trust Registry and this VTC as its trust anchors.

workflow.description: The verify-trust check runs on the repository's pull requests — from a workflow committed to it, or, where the forge supports it, required on it from the namespace's own bridge-managed workflow repository at a pinned commit.

Bootstrap.title: Bootstrap

Did.description: A bare DID in the W3C DID Core syntax (§3.1): `did:`, a method name of lowercase letters and digits, `:`, and a method-specific id of colon-separated segments drawn from `A-Z a-z 0-9 . - _` and percent-encoded octets, the last segment non-empty. A DID URL is not a DID: no path, query or fragment (`/`, `?`, `#`), so a verification-method id such as `did:key:z6Mk…#z6Mk…` is refused. Compared by exact string equality — no case folding or percent-decoding. A consumer MUST still treat the value as data: the pattern keeps shell metacharacters, whitespace and quotes out of the wire form, but it does not make a DID safe to splice into a command or markup.
Did.title: Did

Ext.description: Vendor-namespaced extension object per SPEC.md §4.5.1. Each immediate key MUST be a reverse-DNS namespace; structure under each namespace is opaque to the framework.
Ext.title: Ext

ForgeId.description: An identifier the forge itself assigns — a repository id, a user or organisation id — carried as a string so a forge whose ids are not numbers needs no new version. GitHub, Forgejo and GitLab ids are decimal integers written as strings (`"812736451"`). Unlike a name, it survives renames and transfers, which is why rights and bindings are keyed by it.
ForgeId.title: ForgeId

LastCheck.description: The last verify-trust check run the bridge saw on the repository.

conclusion.description: The check's conclusion, in the forge's words (`success`, `failure`).

LastCheck.title: LastCheck

MappedRole.description: A level of the bridge's forge-neutral role ladder, lowest first: the vocabulary role drift's `observed` and `expected` are reported in. `none` is no direct role on the repository.
MappedRole.title: MappedRole

NamespaceId.description: The VTC's opaque identifier for a namespace, assigned when it is bound. Stable for the life of the binding; never reused for another binding.
NamespaceId.title: NamespaceId

RepoResource.description: A forge-qualified resource naming exactly one repository: `<forge-host>/<owner>/<repo-path>`, lowercase, where the repository path has 1 to 21 segments (see `Resource`).
RepoResource.title: RepoResource

RepoStatus.description: One repository as its administrators govern it: who owns it, how many hold rights on it, how far commit trust is set up, and how its forge compares with the VTC's projection.

checkedAt.description: When the forge was last compared. Absent if never.

committers.description: How many live records of `git.commit.sign` it has. Implied rights are not counted.

createdAt.description: When the VTC first recorded it.

createdBy.description: Who created it through the VTC. Absent for an adopted or unmanaged repository.

driftCount.description: How many drift items are outstanding. The items themselves are in `git-ns/view`.

failedStep.description: The step that failed on the last create or bootstrap.

forgeId.description: The forge's repository id, once confirmed.

guard.description: The guard in force against a pull request satisfying its own check, as the bridge last reported it: `requiredWorkflow`, `codeOwnerReview`, `bridgePostedCheck`, `protectedFiles` or `none`. A client treats any other value as `none`.

id.description: The VTC's identifier for the repository record.

lastError.description: What the bridge said when that step failed.

maintainers.description: How many live records of `git.repo.maintain` it has. Implied rights are not counted.

namespace.description: The namespace it was recorded in. For a `detached` repository, possibly one no longer bound.

owners.description: The DIDs holding a live, explicitly recorded `git.repo.own` on it.

roleMap.description: The forge role each right projects to on this repository under the serving bridge's reported map. Absent while the namespace's map is unknown.

roleMapStale.description: The bridge last projected this repository's roles under an earlier role map, and the re-projection queued for it has not yet succeeded.

steps.description: Per-step outcomes of the last create, bootstrap or inspect job. Empty until one has been reported.

RepoStatus.title: RepoStatus

Response.description: The repositories in the namespaces the caller administers, or in the one asked for.

repos.description: Every repository recorded in an administered namespace, in any state, ordered by `resource`; for a holder of the community-administrator capability without `namespace`, also every repository whose namespace is no longer bound.

Response.title: Git Namespaces — List Repositories — response payload

RoleMap.description: The forge role each repository right is given, as the forge applies it: after the forge's own ladder has rounded it down. `own` is the role `git.repo.own` projects to, `maintain` that of `git.repo.maintain`, `commit` that of `git.commit.sign` (`none` is fork-based contribution). There is no member for `git.ns.admin` or `git.repo.create`, which project to no forge role whatever a bridge is configured with. Ordered: `own` is at least `maintain`, which is at least `commit`, and `commit` is at most `write`.
RoleMap.title: RoleMap

StepOutcome.description: One step of the last create, bootstrap or inspect job on the repository, as the bridge reported it.

detail.description: What the bridge said about it — an error, or why it was skipped.

outcome.description: `applied`, `unchanged`, `failed` or `skipped`. A client shows any other value as reported.

step.description: The step, in the bridge's words (`workflow`, `keyring`, `variables`, `requiredCheck`).

StepOutcome.title: StepOutcome

schema.description: An administrator lists the repositories recorded in the namespaces they administer — every one, for a holder of the community-administrator capability — with owners, right counts, bootstrap, sync and forge status.

namespace.description: Only the repositories in this namespace. It must be one the caller administers; a namespace they do not administer, or one this VTC does not have, is refused with `notAdministrator` alike.

schema.title: Git Namespaces — List Repositories — payload
